clue.text: Beautiful valley west of river, not east

parts.note: a gorge is a narrow steep-sided valley

indicators.note: not means the following letter is left out of the river's name

parts.note: the Ouse is an English river

explanation.surface: Describing a lovely view of a valley lying west of a river.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'west of' means 'placed before'; 'not east' drops the E from the Yorkshire river's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something strikingly attractive to look at, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Boy, it's about time to go to sleep

indicators.note: about means the boy's name goes round the other piece

parts.note: Geoff is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A parent telling a son that bedtime has arrived.
explanation.definitionFit: To drop off into slumber is an informal phrasal-verb sense, as in 'I couldn't nod off'.

clue.text: Be caught in climbing maple to see girl

indicators.note: in means the first pieces sit inside the reversed tree
climbing in a down clue means the tree's name reads upwards

parts.note: Acer is the botanical genus of maples
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Someone climbing a maple tree to catch sight of a girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing' reads the tree upwards as RECA in this down clue; 'in' sets the other letters inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a female forename, so it stands for a girl.

clue.text: Thrill, finding article covered by old coin

parts.note: ex- means former or old

indicators.note: covered by means the article sits inside the coin

parts.note: a cent is a coin
an item is an article, as in an item of clothing

explanation.surface: A collector thrilled to discover an item beneath an ancient coin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'article' tempts as A or THE, but here it means a thing or object; 'covered by' puts it within the coin.
explanation.definitionFit: A thrill is a feeling of intense eagerness or delight, a synonym of the noun.

clue.text: University class taken by local inhabitant, of little use to student?

indicators.note: taken by means the class is held inside the inhabitant

parts.note: a native is someone born in the place
a form is a school class

explanation.surface: A university class taught by a local resident turns out useless to those studying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken by' puts the class inside the inhabitant. The question mark marks a definition by example: an unhelpful lecture tells a student nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that tells a learner nothing new conveys no information, so it is useless for study.

clue.text: Fight army in city of old

parts.note: to spar is to box or fight
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's reserve force

explanation.surface: An army fighting in an ancient city.
explanation.definitionFit: This was a powerful city-state of ancient Greece, so a city of antiquity.

clue.text: Utensils for cooking roasts

definitions.meaning: metal vessels used on the hob for frying or boiling
to roast someone is to criticise them harshly, the same as slating

explanation.surface: Kitchen equipment needed to cook a Sunday roast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roasts' looks like food but is the verb: harsh criticism.
explanation.definitionFit: Saucepans are cooking vessels, and slating a film means criticising it severely.

clue.text: Being more prepared to study, starts off intensive examination revision

parts.note: to read a subject is to study it at university

indicators.note: starts off means the first letters of the following three words are taken

explanation.surface: A student better prepared to study after intensive revision for the exam.
explanation.definitionFit: Readier is the comparative of ready, which means prepared.

clue.text: States Welshman has lost head over nymph

indicators.note: over in a down clue means the first piece sits above the second
lost head means the Welsh name drops its first letter

parts.note: Gareth is a typical Welsh man's name
the USA is the United States

explanation.surface: A Welshman who has lost his head over a nymph.
explanation.walkthrough: 'States' looks like a verb but is USA, which goes under ARETH (GARETH without G).
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth this nymph was turned into a spring, so she is a nymph by name.

clue.text: Bill for America's drug dose?

definitions.meaning: in American English a bill to be paid is called a ...
a tablet, a single dose of a drug such as LSD

explanation.surface: Asking what the American word is for the bill for a dose of drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: A tab is US slang for a bill or check, and short for a tablet of a drug.

clue.text: Such furniture slightly damaged by beer stain finally seeping in

indicators.note: seeping in means the stain's last letter gets inside the damaged piece

parts.note: chipped means slightly damaged, like a cracked plate

indicators.note: finally means the last letter of stain is used

parts.note: ale is a type of beer

explanation.surface: Antique furniture marred by a beer stain that has soaked in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' takes N from 'stain', and 'seeping in' lets it soak into the damaged word, making CHIPPEND.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Chippendale was an 18th-century cabinet-maker whose style names a kind of furniture.

clue.text: The Louvre cinema?

parts.note: the Louvre was once a royal palace and now houses paintings, so taken literally it is a palace for pictures; the phrase is an old name for a cinema

explanation.surface: Wondering whether the great Paris art museum is a film house.
explanation.definitionFit: An old-fashioned British term for a cinema, which the Louvre literally is: a palace of paintings.

clue.text: View of expert given in confrontation

parts.note: a facet is one aspect or view of something
taken as written
an ace is an expert

explanation.surface: An expert's opinion being offered during a dispute.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as FACET-OF-ACE, the letters run together into the answer's two words.
explanation.definitionFit: A meeting eye to eye, in direct opposition, is an idiom for a confrontation.

clue.text: Food that's brought in by steward is hot

indicators.note: brought in by means the letters are carried inside the following words

explanation.surface: A steward bringing in a hot meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A dish is a prepared item of food, as in a tasty dish.

clue.text: Drug addict trading principally in crooked EU emporia

indicators.note: in means the first letter of trading goes inside the rearranged letters
crooked means bent out of shape, so the letters are rearranged
principally means the first letter of trading is taken

explanation.surface: A drug addict doing business in dishonest European shops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crooked' rearranges EU EMPORIA into OPIUMEAER; T, the first letter of 'trading', goes inside before the final ER.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who habitually consumes the poppy drug is an addict, as in De Quincey's Confessions.

clue.text: Defeat for striker

definitions.meaning: to ... an opponent is to beat them heavily

explanation.surface: A football team's goalscorer having to cope with a defeat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'striker' suggests football; here it is a tool that strikes nails.
explanation.definitionFit: To trounce a rival is to thrash them, and the tool hits nails, so it strikes.

clue.text: Military policeman's anger, when blocked by useless officials

indicators.note: when blocked by means the middle pieces are hemmed in by the outer one

parts.note: U/S is short for unserviceable, meaning useless
MP is a military policeman
ire is anger

explanation.surface: A military policeman fuming at incompetent officials.
explanation.walkthrough: U/S, short for unserviceable, is service slang for useless; 'when blocked by' means the policeman and his anger sit between its two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Umpires are the officials who referee cricket or tennis matches.

clue.text: The snake from hell?

parts.note: a pit is a name for hell, so a viper from the pit is literally a hellish snake; the phrase is the name of a real kind of venomous snake

explanation.surface: Asking about a demonic serpent from the underworld.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a family of venomous snakes with heat-sensing pits, and the pit is hell.

clue.text: Kid a member of the Spanish royal family

definitions.text: member of the Spanish royal family

parts.note: a kid is a child or infant

explanation.surface: A child who is one of Spain's royals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kid' looks like a verb, to tease; it is the noun, a child.
explanation.definitionFit: Infanta is the title given to a daughter of the Spanish or Portuguese king.

clue.text: Happen to disagree

definitions.meaning: things that come about or occur, as in 'events fell out badly'
to quarrel and stop being friends

explanation.surface: Two people who happen to argue.
explanation.definitionFit: Events can be said to occur this way, and friends who quarrel do the same.

clue.text: One trade union's impartiality

explanation.surface: Praising a trade union for its fairness.
explanation.walkthrough: Equity is the name of the British trade union for actors.
explanation.definitionFit: It names the actors' union and is the legal and everyday word for fairness.

clue.text: Drink ale -— quit bubbly

indicators.note: bubbly means fizzing and lively, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Someone told to give up ale and champagne for a different drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bubbly' looks like champagne but signals the anagram of ALE and QUIT.
explanation.definitionFit: This Mexican agave spirit is a drink.

clue.text: Exercises briefly, wearing sleeveless garment

indicators.note: briefly means the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: physical jerks are exercises
to be in something is to be wearing it

explanation.surface: Doing quick exercises while dressed in a sleeveless top.
explanation.walkthrough: Physical jerks is a British name for keep-fit exercises.
explanation.definitionFit: A jerkin is a close-fitting sleeveless jacket, a garment.

clue.text: Terrible convict expelled by little community

indicators.note: expelled by means the convict is thrown out of the community

parts.note: a village is a small community
a lag is a convict, as in old lag

explanation.surface: A small village throwing out a dreadful prisoner.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean very bad or awful.

clue.text: Roguish squire with cape blowing about

indicators.note: blowing about means the letters are tossed around

explanation.surface: A rascally country squire whose cloak flaps in the wind.
explanation.definitionFit: Picaresque fiction follows a rogue's adventures, so the word means roguish.

clue.text: Opera that is out of place? Doubly so

indicators.note: doubly so means the result is repeated
out of means the letters are taken out of the word for place

parts.note: lieu means place, as in 'in lieu of'

explanation.surface: An opera that seems out of place, twice over.
explanation.walkthrough: IE taken out of LIEU leaves LU; 'Doubly so' repeats it.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the title of Alban Berg's unfinished opera.

clue.text: Professional soldier, having swallowed potato, is bulging

indicators.note: having swallowed means the vegetable goes inside the other pieces

parts.note: pro is short for professional
a soldier ant is a kind of ant
a potato is a tuber

explanation.surface: A soldier who has eaten a potato and now has a bulging belly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having swallowed' puts the vegetable between the two halves; a soldier is a kind of ant, a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: Protuberant means sticking out or swelling, a synonym of bulging.

clue.text: One starts to loathe knowledgeable type

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: starts to means the first letters of the next two words are taken

explanation.surface: Someone who starts to loathe know-alls.
explanation.definitionFit: Ilk means kind or sort, as in 'people of that ilk'.

clue.text: Give lessons about bottling grand or poor wine?

indicators.note: bottling means the letter is held inside
about means the word is read backwards

parts.note: to tutor is to give lessons
G is short for grand, a thousand pounds

explanation.surface: A teacher bottling a fine or a poor wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reverses TUTOR into ROTUT; G goes inside. The question mark: cheap liquor, not only wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Rotgut is slang for cheap, harsh alcohol such as poor-quality wine.

clue.text: Fruit mother has stored is a kind of apple

parts.note: a pear is a fruit
ma is a familiar word for mother
something stored is kept in

explanation.surface: Mother's store of fruit includes a type of apple.
explanation.definitionFit: The pearmain is an old English apple variety.
